title: Awareness: Lung Cancer Awareness Month (November), $150 low-dose CT lung screening

slides.eyebrow: November is Lung Cancer Awareness Month
slides.title: A yearly low-dose CT can find lung cancer early, before symptoms.
slides.body: In a large national trial, yearly low-dose CT screening lowered lung cancer deaths by about 20% in people at high risk, because it finds cancers while they are still small and treatable.
slides.footnote: Sources: National Cancer Institute (NIH), National Lung Screening Trial; CDC.

slides.title: Yearly screening is advised for adults who:
items: Smoke now, or quit in the last 15 years.
Have no symptoms of lung cancer.
slides.footnote: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force, 2021. The American Cancer Society (2023) also includes former smokers who quit more than 15 years ago. Guidelines differ; ask your doctor. A cough that won't go away or coughing up blood? See your doctor now.

slides.title: In and out.
words: report to you and your doctor
slides.footnote: No fasting. Wear a top without metal. Most findings are small nodules that only need a repeat scan. At our Seminole center, 9555 Seminole Blvd.

slides.title: Good to know
items: Pack-years = packs a day × years smoked.
1 pack a day for 20 years = 20 pack-years.
Screening is once a year while you qualify.
Quitting helps your lungs at any age.

slides.title: Everything included.
items: Many plans cover a yearly screening if you qualify.
slides.footnote: Self-pay price as of October 2026. Using insurance? A doctor's order is needed.

slides.title: Breathe easier.
slides.share: Send this to someone who's been meaning to get checked.
slides.disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Self-pay price as of October 2026. Using Medicare or Medicaid? Ask us what applies.

November is Lung Cancer Awareness Month. Advanced Medical Imaging in Seminole offers low-dose CT lung screening for $150 self-pay, with the radiologist's reading included and no referral needed. A yearly low-dose CT can find lung cancer before symptoms, while it's small and most treatable; in a large national trial it lowered lung cancer deaths by about 20% in people at high risk. The scan takes about 10 minutes with no contrast and no needles, and the report goes to you and your doctor in 48 to 72 hours. The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force advises yearly screening for adults 50 to 80 with a 20 pack-year smoking history who smoke now or quit in the last 15 years; the American Cancer Society also includes people who quit longer ago, so ask your doctor what fits you. Many insurance plans cover a yearly screening if you qualify, with a doctor's order.

Book online at advancedimg.com. General information, not medical advice.
